name: Feel Death
effect: The caster automatically detects any death that occurs within a radius around them and also reveals any undead that fails an MR check.

name: See The Great Beyond
effect: Allows the caster or someone designated by them to see specters and other spiritual creatures invisible to the human eye.

intermediate.description: Spectral beings and Souls awaiting the call

arcane.description: All classes of spirits as well as anything with supernatural characteristics in the area

name: Control Scavengers
effect: Grants the caster control over creatures that feed mostly on the dead. The affected creatures must all be within the specified area and have an individual presence less than 20. Some possible examples include vultures, crows, and maggots.

name: Spectral Shield
effect: Creates a shield of necromantic energy, capable of stopping Spiritual attacks that affect the character’s supernatural resistance, as long as the difficulty is not above the value set by the level of the spell. The spell does not stop any physical attacks.

name: Drain Life
effect: Allows the caster to absorb the life force of another living creature, severely injuring it in the process. The caster must be able to physically touch the target, who must succeed at an MR check or lose a number of life points equal to the level of failure. The caster then adds this amount of life points to their own, however they cannot exceed their normal maximum. Creatures with damage resistance lose 5 times the normal amount, but the caster only restores the normal amount to their own life points. For example, if a damage resistant creature fails by 20 points, they would lose 100 LP, but the caster would only restore 20LP.

name: Necromantic Detection
effect: Allows the caster to detect any living or undead being within a certain radius. Characters may avoid this detection with a successful MR check.

name: Talk to the Dead
effect: Allows the caster to communicate with dead souls and spirits around them, even if they are not aware of the creature’s exact position. The level of the spirit and that of the spell is what determines if the communication is possible.

name: Necromantic Paralysis
effect: Freezes the spiritual essence of undead creatures, rendering them unable to move. Any such being in a radius around the caster is automatically subject to the state of Total Paralysis if they fail an MR check.

name: Necromitude
effect: Allows an undead creature to recover life points supernaturally. It has no effect upon living creatures.

name: Death Beam
effect: Project a strong necromantic discharge. This is an Energy attack with a base damage based on the level of the spell.

name: Raise Corpses
effect: By manipulating necrotic energy, the caster can animate corpses and turn them into zombies or skeletons under their control. The dead do not keep any special abilities or knowledge from their life, as they are merely shells of their former selves. However, they retain natural capabilities, such as natural weapons and some physical characteristics. The power and endurance of the creature varies depending on its body, for example the corpse of a bear is considerably more dangerous than one of a human. Basic information on zombies can be referenced in Anima: Beyond Fantasy – Chapter 25: Common Characters. The caster can raise a number of corpses, as long as their combined presence and individual levels are within the limits set by the spell.

name: Dead Body
effect: Temporarily stops the bodily functions of an individual without killing them, although they are still able to move and act completely normally. As long as the spell remains active, the character will be extremely resistant to the effects of damage and its consequences, so any physical penalty is halved. Additionally, in the state between life and death, it allows the character to remain conscious and ignore penalties (except those caused by criticals). Anyone who inspects the body will be unable to discover that it is not a true corpse. Affects any character up to the level determined by the spell.

name: Drain Magic
effect: Drains the magical energy out of an individual or an object, and transfers it to the caster. Any individual affected by the spell is forced to succeed at an MR check or lose Zeon equal to twice the level of failure, which the caster immediately absorbs.

name: Destroy Undead
effect: Completely destroys the essence of an undead target. Any necromantic enemy targeted by this spell must succeed at an MR check or suffer damage equal to twice the level of failure. Creatures with damage resistance multiply this amount by their damage resistance multiple.

name: Drain Characteristics
effect: By touching a living creature, the caster can absorb one of the individual’s characteristics, increasing their own in the process. The caster must decide the characteristic being drained before executing the spell. The target loses 1 point from this characteristic for every 10 points by which they fail the associated MR check. If the natural value of the characteristic drained is higher than the caster’s, the drained points are absorbed at a one to one ratio. However if the caster has a higher natural value in this characteristic, they must drain 3 points to absorb 1 to their own. These changes last as long as the spell is maintained, and once dismissed the characteristics recover at a rate of 1 point per hour.

name: Control The Dead
effect: The caster obtains absolute control over any undead creature in the area when cast. Dominion over the creatures remains active as long as the spell is maintained, but does not affect any other necromantic creatures that approach later. The creatures can avoid these effects by passing a MR check, and are only allowed another attempt when given an order completely contrary to their nature. As such, creatures without will, such as animated corpses, can never be freed.

name: Wither Life
effect: Creates a necromantic energy area that immediately kills any lesser life form – such as small animals and plants – around the caster. Any living being with a presence less than 20 within the area automatically rots away at a rapid pace, with no ability to make a resistance roll.

name: Necromantic Shield
effect: Creates an energy shield from the essence of dead souls to protect against all manner of attacks.

name: Dominate Life
effect: Allows the caster to enslave a living being’s soul. The victim can resist by succeeding at an MR check, and is allowed a new check each day. The resistance check may also be repeated if given an order completely against their nature.

name: Vampire Stigma
effect: The target of this spell gains the ability to automatically absorb a portion of the damage they personally produce upon their opponents as Life Points. It works on both physical attacks and any spell or mystical power producing direct damage. In the case of damage resistant creatures, this spell absorbs a number of life points equal to damage produced divided by the damage resistance multiple of the creature.

name: Spectral Form
effect: The caster’s body becomes a crackling mass of pure necromantic energy, granting special abilities.

initial.description: The caster is immaterial, and can only be damaged by attacks capable of damaging energy.

intermediate.description: As Base, but those who touch the caster must succeed against an MR or PhR equal to double the caster’s presence, or lose life points equal to half the level of failure.

advanced.description: As Intermediate, but the caster gains Life Points equal to the loss produced by those who touch them.

arcane.description: As Advanced, but if the resistance roll is failed by more than 40, they instantly die.

name: Necromantic Modification
effect: The undead creature that is the target of this spell feeds upon it’s energy, temporarily gaining new powers and abilities. In game terms, an undead obtains a number of additional Development Points to acquire powers and essential abilities described in Anima: Beyond Fantasy – Chapter 26: Creation of Beings. It does so as a creature with Gnosis 25 of the category it currently exists as. A creature can only be affected by one copy of this spell at any time and it’s effects cannot overlap.

name: Summon The Dead
effect: Calls the souls of the dead or specters to the caster. They are able to summon these spirits selectively, although it is possible some other soul may appear in it’s place. Summon the Dead only works upon spirits still awaiting the call, or spectral creatures, with a maximum level based on the level of the spell. It does not affect souls already transmigrated to the Flow of Souls, or those housed in new bodies.

name: Raise Specters
effect: By dominating the souls of the dead, the caster can pervert their essences and turn them into specters in their service. The ghosts keep a small part of the capacities they used to have in life, but lose the majority of their old powers and attributes. A specter raised by this spell reduces to half (rounded up) their level achieved in life. Although it does use the general rule for spiritual creatures, it obtains an additional 100 Development Points to acquire powers deemed appropriate by the caster with Gnosis 20. This spell only works on newly deceased souls who still await the call to the Flow of Souls. It can affect several spirits at the same time, as long as the sum of their presences are within the limit set by the spell.

name: Drain Life Force
effect: Absorbs the life force of an individual and transmits it to whomever is designated by the caster. The character that is to be drained must succeed at an MR check, or lose a point of both Constitution and Power for every 10 points of failure. If the caster wishes, the target may also be aged by this process, by a number of years equal to the level of failure. The absorbed points allow the caster or the subject who receives them to rejuvenate and recover their lost Constitution and Power, up to their natural levels. Characters drained of their vital essence cannot recover it, except through supernatural abilities that allow it (like this one).

name: Kill
effect: Stops a subject’s bodily functions, causing immediate death. It only works on living beings, and is useless against spirits or constructs, who lack vital natural processes to stop. Those affected must succeed at an MR or PhR check to survive.

name: Soul Beam
effect: Projects a magical energy discharge composed of withered souls. The spell is an Energy attack, and only affects beings with a soul. Lifeless physical bodies, such as walls or constructs, are ignored. Given the nature of the attack, only those able to see spirits are able to perceive it.

name: Necromantic Chimera
effect: Creates an undead creature subject to the caster’s control. This entity is developed as a Being Between worlds and Gnosis 25 using the rules described in Anima: Beyond Fantasy – Chapter 26: Creation of Beings. However, the caster cannot create the entity from scratch; in order to develop it, they must gather it’s pieces from several corpses. If looking to endow any power or essential ability, it must find the bodies of those who possessed those powers in life. For example, if wanting to create a creature with natural flight, they must find the corpse of a creature who had that specific ability when alive. The existence of the chimera is linked to the caster’s soul, and as such is subject to the same maximum level rules as the spell Create Being in the path of creation.

name: Life Perversion
effect: Corrupts the essence of a living being and stops its natural bodily functions, immediately transforming it into an undead entity. The afflicted character maintains the same characteristics and abilities they had in life – although their animated corpse status naturally grants them the Physical Exemption power. Individuals may avoid these effects by succeeding at an MR or PhR check.

name: Vassalage
effect: Permanently ties an undead creature’s soul to that of the caster. Thus, the caster automatically becomes it’s hierarchical superior, and the creature’s existence is now fully dependent on the caster. Although this spell does not endow the necromancer with real control over the creature, their essence is tied together such that if the master is destroyed, the creature perishes as well. The affected undead may avoid these effects by succeeding at an MR or PhR check.

name: Drain Souls
effect: The caster plucks the soul of another person, feeding on their essence and power. The stronger the spirit absorbed, the greater energy received. The individual targeted by this spell must succeed at an MR check, or lose an amount of presence equal to half the level of failure. Every five points lost also subtracts a level, and with it any capacity or power that depended upon it. If the target’s presence reaches 0, their soul is completely consumed and they die. For every 10 points of presence absorbed, the caster temporarily increases one of their characteristics by 1, or obtains 10 Development Points to obtain any essential ability or power of a creature with Gnosis 30. Every day, the caster loses 1 of these temporary characteristics, or 20 of the increased Development Points.

name: Surpass Death
effect: Allows a living person to defeat death. In game terms, the target becomes an undead entity without any spiritual ties, and thus can exist in the world on their own power. The spell must be cast at the exact moment of the individuals death – or a few seconds before it (the spell itself does not cause the individual to die). The caster is free to decide if the target in question becomes either a Being Between Worlds or a Spirit, but in either case it acquires a Gnosis of 25. The spell confers a number of extra Development Points to use in acquiring essential abilities and powers described in Anima: Beyond Fantasy – Chapter 26: Creation of Beings. If the caster chooses for the target to become a Spirit, the target must spend 100 of the Development Points gained to that end. Excess development points grant additional levels, as well as other effects described in the spell Chimera in the path of creation. Since this spell only affects living beings, it cannot be used on creatures already of a necromantic nature.

initial.description: +100 DP, with up to 100 DP of disadvantages.

intermediate.description: +200 DP, with up to 100 DP of disadvantages.

advanced.description: +300 DP, with up to 200 DP of disadvantages.

arcane.description: +400 DP, with up to 200 DP of disadvantages.

name: True Rise
effect: Raises a corpse allowing it to maintain it’s knowledge and every one of it’s powers and abilities it had in life. Unfortunately, the raised creature becomes an undead that lacks a true soul. The spell affects deceased creatures or characters with a maximum level based on the level of the spell, and whose bodies are within reach of the caster. If death occurred a long time before the spell is cast, the raised creature’s physical abilities might be damaged. Characters resurrected once through this spell can not be resurrected again. As well, even though it is an undead entity, it retains it’s free will and is not under the caster’s control.

name: Well of Life
effect: Creates a field of dark energy centered on the necromancer that allows them to absorb half of all lost life points of living beings within a radius around them. These life points go toward healing any sort of wound they have incurred. Well of Life itself does not inflict any damage, but typically casters incorporate this spell with other damaging magics at their disposal.

name: Cursed Land
effect: By corrupting a small fragment of the world, the caster enchants an area of land, causing any being that dies within to rise instantly as an undead under their control. The deceased automatically become animated corpses, although powerful beings with Gnosis at least 5 points above their Natura, rise as a Specter instead (as if it had been affected by the spell Raise Specter). Creatures can only act while inside of the cursed land. If they leave it’s area, the magic that sustains them disappears, and they die. Once cast, the area affected remains stationary.

name: Sustenance
effect: Affects the essence of one or several undead maintained by the caster, allowing for their existence after the caster stops maintaining their existence. For example, if the caster uses Sustenance upon an animated corpse from the spell Raise Corpses, the creature will continue to ‘live’ once the spell has ended. The caster may affect as many undead as desired, as long as their total presence is within the limit set by the spell.

name: Raw Material
effect: Generates the corrupting energy used by necromancy to resurrect corpses and spirits, enabling the caster to create the raw material necessary to resurrect as corpses at a later stage. The spell forms the necromantic materials, equivalent to a number of human bodies based on the level of the spell. In the case of other, more powerful creatures, a smaller number is used instead based on the GM’s discretion.

name: Lord of the Dead
effect: The caster extends their presence over a large area of the world, subduing all undead creatures in a large area. All such creatures within the area must succeed at an MR check or be subject to the complete control of the caster. If failed, no additional attempts to escape are possible, unless the base resistance value of the creature changes.

name: Come Back From The Dead
effect: Returns a deceased creature’s spirit to the world, even after it has returned to the flow of souls or if their essence has been dispersed. The creature returns as an undead being, but keeps their soul and essence intact. If the body of the deceased still exists, it returns to it. If it does not exist, they may return to a new one provided or become an immaterial specter. As is the case in similar spells, the level of the entity and the time since their death are limiting factors for this spell. Souls that have been utterly destroyed or since resurrected after death can not be affected.

name: The Awakening
effect: The most powerful of the necromantic spells. By corrupting a part of the soul of the world, the caster extends their shadow throughout existence, returning life to the dead and submitting them to the caster’s dominion. The awakening does not have a certain range of action; it equally affects any deceased whose level was not higher than described by the level of the spell. If their spirit still awaits the call, they rise as specters, otherwise as animated corpses. Those beings who have a Gnosis 15 points above their Natura, return as undead with all of their faculties and abilities.
